evidence.summary: An employee submits an expense claim.
Accounts Payable checks receipts and returns incomplete claims to the employee.
The line manager approves business purpose.
Claims above EUR 2,000 additionally require the finance controller.
Accounts Payable pays approved claims and informs the employee.
Rejected claims end with a notice.

issues.description: What is the required order or coordination of line-manager and finance-controller approvals, and who evaluates the amount threshold? The snapshot keeps the additional controller rule and payment segment disconnected from manager approval so no approval ordering is asserted. Payment requires all applicable approvals; the controller is additional, never a substitute for the manager.

After Accounts Payable returns an incomplete claim, does the employee correct and resubmit it, and where does it re-enter? The current segment ends at return; this is a scope boundary, not an asserted terminal claim outcome.

Which review decisions can reject a claim, and who issues the rejection notice to whom? The rejected-claim notice is a separate supported segment with unspecified responsibility; no reviewer rejection branch or notification owner is invented.

links.assertion: Entry boundary of the supported submission segment.
The employee submits the claim.
Accounts Payable checks receipts.
Accounts Payable distinguishes incomplete claims during receipt checking.
Accounts Payable returns incomplete claims to the employee.
This segment stops at the evidenced return. The claim lifecycle and any resubmission remain unresolved.
The line manager approves business purpose. This segment shows the positive approval action; rejection routing is not specified.
This segment ends with the stated manager approval. It does not assert that reimbursement or all required approvals are complete.
Begin the supported submission segment.
Receipt checking follows claim submission.
Receipt checking determines whether the claim is incomplete.
Incomplete claims are returned.
The known segment ends after the return, without inventing rework.
Complete claims proceed to business-purpose approval in the procedure narrative.
The manager approval segment concludes with business purpose approved.
Entry boundary for the additional-approval rule, independent of any unconfirmed ordering relative to manager review.
The stated additional controller requirement applies strictly above EUR 2,000. The evaluating role is unspecified.
The finance controller provides the additional approval required above EUR 2,000.
The supported controller approval segment ends here; this is not full claim approval.
The stated amount rule does not require controller approval for EUR 2,000 or below; manager approval is still required.
Apply the source amount rule without assigning an unsupported evaluating owner.
A claim above EUR 2,000 requires controller approval in addition to line-manager approval.
Claims at or below EUR 2,000 do not require the additional controller approval under this rule.
Conclude the supported positive controller approval segment.
The payment segment starts only with an approved claim; above EUR 2,000 both named approvals are required. Approval orchestration is unresolved.
Accounts Payable pays approved claims.
Accounts Payable informs the employee after paying the approved claim.
The source payment and notification actions are complete.
Only approved claims enter the payment action.
Accounts Payable pays the claim and informs the employee.
The payment segment concludes after the employee is informed.
Entry boundary at the explicitly stated rejected-claim state; who rejects and the decision routes remain unspecified.
A rejected claim ends with a notice. The notice owner and recipient are not specified.
Rejected claims conclude with a notice.
A rejected claim receives a notice.
The rejected claim ends with the notice.
Preserve the distinct source role: Employee.
Preserve the distinct source role: Accounts Payable.
Preserve the distinct source role: Line manager.
Preserve the distinct source role: Finance controller.
Unassigned responsibility is displayed without attributing it to Accounts Payable or either approver.
